## 72d67c0cf1b7

**Finding: repeated-color components are never generated, so a color-class shortcut survives.** Every ordinary draw assigns a distinct color to each isolated motif, and all three canonical inputs also use each foreground color for exactly one component. Therefore a rival that groups all cells of a color into one global bbox and rotates that color class once fits the supplied curriculum, even though the intended rule rotates each connected component independently.

Concrete counterexample (0 background): put color 2 at `(1,1),(2,1),(2,2)` and also at `(4,4),(4,5),(4,6)` in a 7×8 grid. The intended rule rotates the first L within its 2×2 bbox to `(1,1),(1,2),(2,1)` and the second horizontal line within its 1×3 bbox to the vertical line `(4,4),(5,4),(6,4)`. A per-color/global-bbox rival rotates the six cells together and produces different coordinates. The current generator cannot emit this because it samples distinct colors without replacement and `self_check` rejects repeated motif colors.
